title: Interaction Payload Contracts PRD and Soft-Launch Checklist
creator: Mariana Gomez
description: Purpose: Define a compact, predictable payload contract and acceptance criteria for the hosted interaction endpoints (chat, completion, embeddings, rerank) focused on first-mile reliability and smooth customer migration. This PRD clarifies minimal surface guarantees, required telemetry, data retention boundaries, and a staged soft-launch plan targeted at early enterprise adopters.
scope: In-scope: API request/response shapes for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank, streaming semantics, function-call metadata, structured output schemas, error surface and retry guidance, rate-limit headers, and telemetry hooks. Out-of-scope: multi-tenant billing UI, dedicated capacity autoscaling controls, advanced query planner for cross-model routing.
scope_changes: Initial scope included model family auto-fallback (A/B at runtime). To reduce launch risk, fallback implementation is deferred to post-soft-launch (post-2026-Q2). Also limited the initial model catalog to three verified variants for each endpoint instead of broad set to shrink verification matrix.
requirements: REQ-1: Request and response JSON schemas must be versioned and published under /v1/specs with migration notes.
REQ-2: Chat must support streaming (EventStream) and single-message completion; both flows must include consistent token-level latency metrics.
REQ-3: Embeddings endpoint returns a fixed-length numeric vector and a stable idempotency token when same input repeated within 5 minutes.
REQ-4: Rerank accepts an array of up to 200 candidates and returns a ranked index array; rank stability metric must be computed in eval harness.
REQ-5: All endpoints must emit standard X-Request-ID and rate-limit headers (X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset).
REQ-6: Structured output contract: when schema=structured, response must validate against provided JSON Schema or return a 422 with validation errors.
REQ-7: Function-calling interactions include a function_name, arguments (JSON object), and confidence metadata (0.0-1.0).
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Published API schemas (stable v1) with example requests/responses for every endpoint and path. Documentation review approval from DX (developer experience).

AC-2: End-to-end smoke tests pass for chat stream, chat non-stream, completion, embeddings, and rerank in three regions (us-west1, us-east1, eu-west1) with <5% error rate during synthetic traffic runs.
AC-3: Token latency SLO: p95 < 250ms for streaming token emission under baseline load (100 r/s per model lane).
AC-4: Observability: dashboards show per-route latency, error breakdown, tokenized cost estimate, and a synthetic workload probe for each endpoint that runs every 5 minutes.
AC-5: Safety: responses that trigger configured safety checks return structured rejection objects and generate an incident metric. Safety handling verified by Compliance reviewer.
AC-6: Backwards compatibility validation: a compatibility test suite validates that existing SDK examples still function and fail with clear migration guidance when not compatible.
AC-7: Security review completed and KMS integration validated for any customer-provided keys used during private deployments.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal canary (redwood-dev org) for two weeks. Phase 1: Soft-launch to 5 enterprise pilot customers with dedicated runbook and increased telemetry retention. Phase 2: Gradual increase to open self-serve with rate limiting tiers and an opt-in telemetry contract. Post-launch: enable fallback routing and expanded model catalog.

notes: Design decisions: 1) Use conservative default rate-limits on soft-launch to protect SLOs. 2) Require explicit schema=structured header for structured outputs to keep backward compatibility. 3) Defer dynamic model fallback until after pilot to reduce cross-team testing surface.
